scope: Comparative critical review of synthetic genome takeover, minimal-cell division rescue and inherited minimal-cell adaptation versus de novo abiotic cell bootstrapping; research only
existing_living_cell_descendant_replicat: yes (2010, 2021, 2023), but distinct from de novo construction

studies.citation: Gibson DG et al. Creation of a Bacterial Cell Controlled by a Chemically Synthesized Genome. Science 329:52-56 (2010).
studies.grade: E2 accessible original main Methods/Results/Discussion narrative; no supplemental/raw evidence reanalysis
studies.rights: AAAS 2010 copyrighted original; no verified blanket CC licence; paraphrase only
studies.research_program: J Craig Venter Institute, overlaps P45-S2 and P45-S3 collaborators
positive: Approximately 1.08 Mbp synthetic M. mycoides genomic DNA assembled using synthetic fragments and yeast intermediates
Transplanted into living M. capricolum recipient, recipient genome replaced; donor-type self-replicating descendants with synthetic watermarks
Author-reported colony outgrowth beyond 30 generations implies dilution of founding cytoplasm >10^9-fold
negative: Initial unmethylated genome transplantation failed against recipient DNA restriction until compatible protection/bypass conditions
Single-base deletion in essential dnaA delayed successful functional synthetic genome
Synthetic genome mostly encoded known viable natural bacterial functions rather than novel engineered de novo life
external_support: Initially living recipient cytoplasm with membranes, active enzymes and translation machinery
Externally engineered, assembled and transplanted chromosome
Researcher quality control, restriction-system handling and nutrients
studies.experimental_unit: One successful constructed genome/recipient system with laboratory colony multiplication; total independent successful donor/recipient bootstraps not verified
studies.limitation: Genome-directed living descendants are not proof of the initial assembly of cellular life from nonliving materials
studies.conflicts_of_interest: Science original disclosed JCVI/Synthetic Genomics Inc. ownership, executive roles and related patent applications

studies.citation: Pelletier JF et al. Genetic requirements for cell division in a genomically minimal cell. Cell 184:2430-2440.e16 (2021).
studies.grade: E1 original published abstract and institutional submitted-version abstract, not published complete Methods/Results
studies.rights: Published Cell article under Elsevier user license; MIT-submitted original manuscript lists CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for that manifestation only; no figure/content redistribution
studies.research_program: JCVI with MIT and NIST, overlaps 2010 and 2023 collaborators
positive: Irregular propagation morphology observed in JCVI-syn3.0 using microfluidic culture
Adding 19 genes yielded syn3A near-normal morphology
Seven jointly required for parental-like morphological restoration, including ftsZ, sepF, one hydrolase and four membrane-related unknown-function genes
negative: Genomically viable syn3.0 nevertheless displayed irregular cell morphology
Intermediate or individually failed combinations, denominators and quantitative effects were not verified from complete original full text in this pass
external_support: Researcher-designed gene additions and strain engineering
Microfluidic medium perfusion and laboratory growth conditions
Existing living minimal-cell lineage and functioning natural Mycoplasma cellular machinery
studies.experimental_unit: Exact line counts and observation denominators not verified from abstract-only access
studies.limitation: Joint normal-morphology rescue cannot be promoted to necessity of every gene for any viable replication or de novo bottom-up origin

studies.citation: Moger-Reischer RZ et al. Evolution of a minimal cell. Nature 620:122-127 (2023).
studies.grade: E2 full accessible original publisher main methods/results/figure descriptions/discussion; no raw data/code/supplement replication
studies.rights: CC BY 4.0 original publisher, third-party exclusions; paraphrase only
studies.research_program: Indiana University/Lennon/Lynch collaboration with JCVI Glass/Wise/Sun; same ancestor program as 2010/2021
studies.strain_background: JCVI-syn3B 493 genes versus syn1.0 901 genes; syn3B restored 19 genes, has extra rRNA operon, efflux deletion and manipulation site; not syn3.0
positive: Four independently propagated populations per strain were serially maintained ~1997 estimated generations across 300 days
Competition mean evolved minimal fitness 0.998 vs ancestor nonminimal 1.00, t-test P=0.957 (non-significant difference not proven equality)
Relative-fitness adaptation estimated 39% faster for minimal than nonminimal cell (P=0.032)
Mutation rates ~3 x 10^-8 per nucleotide per generation, not elevated due to minimization
negative: Genome minimization caused 57% initial maximum-growth reduction and 53% initial competition fitness reduction
Minimal-cell size remained essentially unchanged despite large non-minimal diameter increase (t-test P=0.181)
No membrane-transport gene mutation enrichment difference P=0.934, biosynthesis enrichment only marginal P=0.090
external_support: Daily operator-managed 1% fresh SP4 liquid serial transfers at 37 C in dark static cultures
Preexisting living founder cells, physiological rich medium and 300 days maintenance
Researcher-handled competitions, cytometry, microscopy and genetic sequencing
studies.experimental_unit: n=4 independently evolved lineages per strain; n=87 and 57 mutation accumulation lines; single ancestor clone per strain, n=4 ancestral technical fitness measurements
studies.limitation: Demonstrates inherited adaptive fitness in living cells; does not demonstrate abiotic cell bootstrapping, self-managed new ecological establishment or universal environment fitness

correction.note: Corrected one author affiliation and duplicated Extended Data Table 2 which had repeated Table 3; current online versions updated

causal_distinctions: Synthetic genome bootstrapped by viable living recipient versus abiotic cytoplasm/cell assembly
Real descendant self-reproduction versus operator-controlled genome engineering at the initial founder
Division morphology restoration versus de novo functional origin
Adaptation of extant lineage in rich lab medium versus new heritable ecological function, unattended dispersal or colonization
review_limitations: Cell 2021 grade remains E1 due to lack of accessible full peer-reviewed Methods and Results
2010 and 2023 primary main texts reviewed but raw sources and supplementary methods not reanalyzed
Three different experiments with overlapping institutional/author founder lineages do not form independent E3 replications of abiotic cellular origin
2023 publisher correction noted but corrected raw table values not independently checked
release_gate: Exact reviewed PR head CI green plus unchanged main prior to expected-head merge and successful separate post-merge main push workflow; interactive write does not establish scheduled-write grant
